beaches.name: Port Erin
beaches.description: A gorgeous sheltered bay on the southwest coast. Sandy beach with calm waters ideal for families. Victorian promenade, cafes, and the steam railway terminus nearby.

beaches.name: Peel Beach
beaches.description: Wide sandy beach backed by the famous Peel Castle. The best surf beach on the island with consistent Atlantic swells. Sunsets here are spectacular.

beaches.name: Ramsey Mooragh Park Beach
beaches.description: Long stretch of sand on the northeast coast near Ramsey. Backed by Mooragh Park with its boating lake. Safe swimming, popular with families.

beaches.name: Port Soderick
beaches.description: A hidden gem — small rocky cove accessible by steam railway or cliff walk. No road access makes it delightfully quiet. Good snorkelling in clear waters.

beaches.name: Niarbyl
beaches.description: Remote, wild and breathtakingly beautiful. Shingle and rock beach with dramatic geology. Not for swimming but unmissable for scenery. Featured in 'Waking Ned'.

beaches.name: Douglas Beach
beaches.description: The town beach stretching along Douglas Bay. Shingle and sand. Convenient for town visitors. The horse trams run alongside. Good for an evening stroll.

beaches.name: Gansey / Port St Mary
beaches.description: Sheltered south-facing beach with excellent swimming. The clear shallow water warms up in summer. Popular with local families. Good cafe nearby.
beaches.dogRestrictions: Dogs welcome all year on main beach

beaches.name: Laxey Beach
beaches.description: A shingle beach at the mouth of the Laxey River. Combine with a visit to the Laxey Wheel nearby. The Manx Electric Railway stops right here.
